findings.trigger: Submitting a case status transition or Four-Eyes signoff without optimistic concurrency tokens, or receiving HTTP 409 Conflict from backend when case version changed concurrently.
findings.expected_behavior: Frontend must send expected_status, expected_version, and expected_timeline_hash with mutations. On HTTP 409 Conflict, optimistic state must be rolled back, ['case', caseId] and ['cases'] must be invalidated and refetched, and the user must receive truthful conflict feedback.
findings.actual_behavior: CaseDetailPage previously omitted expected_status, expected_version, and expected_timeline_hash. In catch blocks, queryClient cache was not invalidated, leaving stale local state un-reconciled.
findings.backend_truth: backend/app/presentation/routers/cases.py enforces strict lost update prevention (HTTP 409) and stale approval checks via expected_version and expected_timeline_hash.
findings.user_visible_impact: User could see out-of-sync case state after concurrent supervisor updates or failed transitions.
findings.tenant_impact: Isolated per case; risk of lost updates across concurrent analyst sessions.
findings.business_impact: Stale case decisions could conflict with authoritative backend audit trail.
findings.root_cause: Omission of concurrency token propagation in mutation payloads and lack of error-time cache invalidation.
findings.repair: Added version and timeline_hash to Case types, added expected_status, expected_version, expected_timeline_hash to CaseStatusUpdatePayload/CaseSignPayload/CaseResolvePayload, and added onError cache invalidations to useUpdateCaseStatus, useSignCase, and useResolveCase.

findings.trigger: Opening a case resolved as closed_false_positive or an unreviewed open case and viewing the SAR export button.
findings.expected_behavior: FinCEN SAR XML export button must be disabled for closed_false_positive and unreviewed cases with clear explanatory tooltips reflecting backend business rule BIZ-0005.
findings.actual_behavior: Button was only disabled during active XML export (disabled={isExportingXml}), leaving it clickable for false-positive cases.
findings.backend_truth: backend/app/presentation/routers/cases.py rejects SAR filing generation for CLOSED_FALSE_POSITIVE and unreviewed cases with HTTP 400 upfront.
findings.user_visible_impact: Users were presented with an actionable SAR export button on false positive cases that resulted in confusing runtime failure upon click.
findings.business_impact: Contradicted AML compliance rules preventing regulatory SAR filing synthesis for confirmed non-fraud events.
findings.root_cause: UI button disabled condition failed to incorporate isFincenEligible check.
findings.repair: Updated button to disabled={isExportingXml || !isFincenEligible} with state-specific tooltips and status badges.

findings.trigger: Switching active tenant in browser context while query cache is populated.
findings.expected_behavior: Switching tenant must immediately purge cached data from Tenant A to prevent any leakage or momentary display under Tenant B.
findings.actual_behavior: Tenant ID was stored in localStorage without an explicit cache-clearing switch helper, relying solely on logout.
findings.backend_truth: Backend enforces strict tenant isolation and BOLA checks on all endpoints.
findings.user_visible_impact: Potential momentary visual leakage of Tenant A case or alert data if tenant context changed without page reload.
findings.tenant_impact: Cross-tenant data exposure in client memory.
findings.root_cause: Absence of coordinated cache-purge helper on tenant context switch.
findings.repair: Exported getActiveTenantId, setClientTenant, and switchActiveTenant(queryClient, newTenantId) which invokes queryClient.clear().

findings.trigger: Accessing Webhook Gateway controls, testing webhook dispatch, or observing SSRF validation errors.
findings.expected_behavior: Operators must have a dedicated security tab to register webhooks with clear SSRF warnings (RFC 1918 / loopback / cloud metadata), dispatch synthetic test events, and inspect real outbound delivery logs with truthful success/failure diagnostics.
findings.actual_behavior: SecurityPage lacked a dedicated Webhook Gateway tab and queries.ts lacked useWebhookTestDispatchMutation.
findings.first_divergence: SecurityPage.tsx tab definitions and queries.ts hook omissions.
findings.user_visible_impact: Inability for operators to verify webhook endpoints or observe SSRF rejections in the UI.
findings.tenant_impact: Webhook management required direct curl calls without UI parity.
findings.business_impact: Reduced visibility into automated notification delivery and security filtering.
findings.root_cause: Omission of webhook UI surfaces from SecurityPage.
findings.repair: Added useWebhookTestDispatchMutation to queries.ts, added 'webhooks' security tab in SecurityPage with registration, SSRF notice, test dispatch, and delivery audit log viewer.
